verdict: PASS at source-review scope. M2056 additively repairs all four M2054 P0s and all four M2054 P1s without modifying the sealed predecessor: each axis filelist contains exactly its M2029 mapped Verilog; ascending unpacked banks and lanes are bridged using DC's high-segment element-zero convention; global full40 slot 42 is locked to M2047 anchor slot 0 and all frozen identity, work, cache, request, preload, and cycle values are asserted; every active measurement clock rejects mapped public X/Z; UCLI has exactly two measurement stops plus a final run to the frozen M2051 PASS; and PTPX derives design, strip scope, and cycles from one axis while loading both SSG and TT before the mapped SDC. No VCS, SAIF, PTPX, compiler, or license command was run. These hashes authorize construction and independent source review of an exact-SHA, no-retry one-shot runner; they do not authorize execution of an unwritten runner or constitute functional, timing, power, or energy evidence.

p2_findings: No exact-SHA one-shot runner exists in this reviewed source set. Its author may not add sources, accept arbitrary WORKLOAD_SLOT values, alter the top/UCLI/PTPX identity, retry automatically, or execute before a separate runner source hammer.

The selected activity mask is real ep34 capture data, but the frozen M2051 memory returns deterministic directed INT8 weights and selected measured nonzeros are positive. Any eventual energy receipt remains a single component workload and is not real-weight, empirically bipolar, full-FC, network, or system energy.
